analysis_notes.source_text_analysis: Torah #232 reads: 'When one recites: Praise the Lord from the heavens, etc., praise Him all His angels, praise Him all His hosts, etc. — the person calls to all of them and commands them all to praise the Lord. From this, a person should be aroused to prayer with heartfelt intention, since in his prayer he calls to all the worlds to praise and glorify Him, may He be blessed.' The text mentions the following concepts: תפלה (prayer), כוונת הלב (kavvanah / heartfelt intention), עולמות (worlds), מלאכים (angels), צבאות (hosts), הלל ושבח (praise and glorification). NONE of these appear in bechina-equivalence language. The word 'בחינת' does not appear in the text. All relationships in this teaching are observational or motivational in structure: the fact that prayer commands all worlds to praise God motivates the person to pray with kavvanah. This is an eitza chain (observation about the scope of prayer → arousal to focused prayer), not a bechina web. Therefore there are no missing bechina nodes to flag, and no additions to propose.
